faqs.q: Is Dokkiman's PDF editor free?
faqs.a: Yes. You can edit and download PDFs without an account. A free account adds a Document Manager and more daily use; paid plans add more.

faqs.q: Can I change the text that's already in a PDF?
faqs.a: Yes. Choose Edit text and click a line to change it. A scanned PDF is a picture of text, so it has no text to change: use White-out and Add text instead.

faqs.q: What's the difference between white-out and redact?
faqs.a: White-out covers something with white, but what's underneath stays in the file. Redact removes the text and images underneath when you save, so they can't be recovered.

faqs.q: Do you keep my files?
faqs.a: No. Your file is edited and sent straight back to you. It's only kept if you choose Save to Document Manager.

faqs.q: Can I edit a Word document or a photo?
faqs.a: Yes. Word documents (.docx) and photos (JPG, PNG or WebP) are turned into a PDF when you open them, so you can edit them like any other PDF.

faqs.q: Are Dokkiman signatures legally binding?
faqs.a: Yes, for most contracts and agreements. In the US, the ESIGN Act and UETA give electronic signatures the same legal effect as handwritten ones when the signer means to sign and the signed record is kept. When you send a document for others to sign with Request Signatures, each signer agrees to sign electronically and you get a Certificate of Completion as evidence. In the EU, UK, Canada and Australia, electronic signatures are also valid for most contracts; Dokkiman's are simple electronic signatures, not the qualified signatures a few EU documents require. This is general information, not legal advice.

faqs.q: Which documents can't be signed electronically?
faqs.a: In the US: wills, codicils and testamentary trusts; adoption, divorce and other family-law papers; court orders and official court documents; notices of utility shut-off, foreclosure or eviction, and cancellation of health or life insurance; and documents that must be notarized. Some deeds, recordings and promissory notes have their own rules too. Other countries have similar lists, so check for yours.

faqs.q: Can I sign a Word document?
faqs.a: Yes. Open a Word document (.docx) and it's turned into a PDF, so the layout can't shift, then sign it or send it for signature like any PDF. You download the signed copy as a PDF.

faqs.q: Do the people I send a document to need an account?
faqs.a: No. They get an email with a private link, open the document and sign it in their browser.

faqs.q: Is signing free?
faqs.a: Signing a PDF yourself is free. Sending documents for others to sign is included in the free trial and in the Basic and Pro plans.

faqs.q: What's in the audit trail?
faqs.a: Who signed, when, from which IP address, and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the document before and after signing, so any later change can be spotted.

faqs.q: Are Dokkiman signatures legally binding?
faqs.a: Yes, for most contracts and agreements. In the US, the ESIGN Act and UETA give electronic signatures the same legal effect as handwritten ones when the signer means to sign, agrees to sign electronically, and the signed record is kept. Dokkiman records each of these: signers tick a box agreeing to sign electronically before they finish, and every signed document comes with a Certificate of Completion. In the EU, UK, Canada and Australia, electronic signatures are also valid for most contracts; Dokkiman's are simple electronic signatures, not the qualified signatures a few EU documents require. This is general information, not legal advice.

faqs.q: Which documents can't be signed electronically?
faqs.a: In the US: wills, codicils and testamentary trusts; adoption, divorce and other family-law papers; court orders and official court documents; notices of utility shut-off, foreclosure or eviction, and cancellation of health or life insurance; and documents that must be notarized. Some deeds, recordings and promissory notes have their own rules too. Other countries have similar lists, so check for yours.

faqs.q: What proves who signed?
faqs.a: Each signer gets their own private link by email, so signing shows they had access to that email address. The Certificate of Completion lists every step (sent, opened, signed or declined) with the time, IP address and browser, plus SHA-256 fingerprints of the document before and after signing, so any later change shows. The signed PDF and certificate are emailed to everyone and kept in your Document Manager.

faqs.q: Will compressing lower the quality?
